cim: A petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO tops 100K signatures, including Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney, and Garry Tan; organizers say 5K+ Nvidia staff signed (Lauren Edmonds/Business Insider)
cim_eredeti: A petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO tops 100K signatures, including Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney, and Garry Tan; organizers say 5K+ Nvidia staff signed (Lauren Edmonds/Business Insider)
szoveg_eredeti:
Some people aren't ready to let former CEO Jensen Huang go.

A petition to reinstate Huang as Nvidia's CEO has some 97,000 signatures as of Saturday morning, including prominent tech leaders such as billionaire Elon Musk and Replit CEO Amjad Masad. Both executives promoted the petition on X.

A website for the campaign, dubbed "Stand with Jensen," said the list includes more than 51,000 shareholders, more than 5,100 current Nvidia employees, and nearly 900 former employees.

It also, to be fair, included "Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor" and "Xi Jingping," a possibly misspelled reference to the Chinese leader. In an X post on Saturday, the organizers said they were "actively working" to remove fake signatures.

This is the letter @elonmusk signed, please read it and consider adding your name too. 💚 https://t.co/yQcJEkUtXO

Earlier this week, Nvidia's board of directors said it opened an investigation into whether Huang was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort" after he admitted to having an affair in a letter to staffers. Days later, Huang resigned after reports he had another affair with an Nvidia executive, and the board appointed Colette Kress, executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO until they find a permanent successor.

An October report by The New York Times said Huang had developed a "close relationship" with Alice Huang, a tech executive at Megaspeed in Singapore. The Times reported that US intelligence officials said she may be a spy for the Chinese government. China has since denied that claim. On Thursday, Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Department of Justice had not concluded whether Alice Huang was a spy.

The "Stand with Jensen" organizers said in an open letter to Nvidia's board posted to its website that they believe the board removed Huang without an investigation and "meaningful due process."

"We have not been shown evidence substantiating the espionage allegation. After thirty-three years pouring his heart and soul into NVIDIA, Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice," they said.

The organizers say they want Huang to remain CEO while the investigation continues.

"Disclose its scope and timeline, give him a meaningful opportunity to respond, and provide a clear, evidence-based explanation demonstrating that any removal is in NVIDIA's best interests. The campaign does not treat espionage allegations as proven facts or presume the inquiry's findings," the organizers said.

The "Stand with Jensen" petition also garnered signatures from big names such as Boom Supersonic CEO Blake Scholl and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan. A signatory who describes himself as an engineer at Nvidia called Huang an "essential part" of the company in a comment on the website.

"His private affairs are none of my business, and if his actions violated our code of conduct, it has to be dealt with. Please bring him back and give him fair treatment, taking his track record and importance for NVIDIA and the wider community into account," the employee said.

In a statement, Nvidia's board of directors said it will consider internal and external candidates in its quest to replace Huang, who cofounded the company and served as CEO for over three decades. The board has not publicly identified a new CEO, but the names of potential candidates have begun to surface among analysts and investors.
